summary: Watch. Micron is a sound business on the rule (FY2026 ROIC 110.54% against a 9.37% discount rate), but none of the three claims is Supported. C1 (core, mature margin at least the own 27.645% median, tested as TTM operating margin of at least 50% through FY2028) rests on contracted evidence, $134bn of remaining performance obligations at minimum pricing, but those cover a minority of revenue, and a 2019-style first downturn year applied to today's 80.68% quarterly margin lands near 51.5%. That makes it Contested at 0.45. C2 (TTM operating income at least $99.34bn through FY2028) and C3 (TTM operating cash flow less capex at least $52.99bn) are Contested too: guidance and consensus support them near term, but the past cycles turned within two years of a peak. The severe peak-earnings flag stays unresolved. Both macro conditions hold. The mispricing does not hold: the price is 5.3% under the base-case DCF value and the market's fade has history behind it. The effective base case is the code's, at 7.46% a year.

rulings.reasoning: The evidence row shows TTM operating margin at 74.586% against a 50% test and a 46.28% kill (prep evidence 0): the test passes today and the kill is far off. The guided and consensus November and February quarters keep the TTM above 50% well into 2027. So the claim turns on FY2028, the four quarters to August 2028. The contracted evidence is real: $134bn of remaining performance obligations at committed volumes and minimum pricing, about 25% due within twelve months, backed by $12.75bn of deposits and $7bn of letters of credit. The 10-K says floor-price gross margins should be above any past cycle's peak quarterly margin. But the 10-K also says these obligations are not indicative of future revenue. The company's own estimate, relayed by a secondary source, puts the agreements at over 35% of revenue through 2030, so most revenue still follows market prices, which went to a -9.1% gross margin in FY2023. The base rate argues against a structural change. In the first downturn year after the 2018 peak, the margin kept 64% of its level (49.34% to 31.51%). The same ratio applied to the August 2026 quarter's 80.68% gives about 51.5%, right on the test line. A 2023-style fall (31.54% to -36.97%) breaks it outright. R1 (shortage price) and R3 (supply from Samsung, CXMT and Micron's own Idaho fab from mid-2027, inside the test window) are not answered by the contracts. Depreciation from capex of $30.7bn in FY2026 and about $25bn in the first half of FY2027 alone also weighs on the margin. If FY2028 is not a downturn year the claim passes, and the contracts cushion a mild one. I put that at a little under even. The contracted evidence does not make the claim more likely than not, so it is Contested, not Supported.

TTM operating income is $99.34bn, exactly the test line, and the kill is $85bn (prep evidence 1). The near term is firmly for the claim. The November 2025 quarter's $6.14bn drops out next, against consensus November-quarter revenue of $61.74bn and the August quarter's $43.75bn of operating income, so FY2026 is not the trailing peak. Consensus revenue is $275.51bn for FY2027 and $319.68bn for FY2028. The binding test is FY2028, which needs about a quarter of today's run-rate per quarter, roughly $25bn. That threshold is far below consensus, which is why this is more likely than not. History argues against calling it Supported. FY2019 operating income fell to about half of FY2018's, and a similar fall from a FY2027 near consensus lands close to $99bn. The 2022-23 downturn cut TTM EBIT 81% in three quarters (R1's precedent), and that would fail it. R3 (supply arriving 2027-28) and R4 (data-centre concentration, a 17.5% one-day fall on build-out fears) are not answered beyond consensus. R6 (Taiwan labour, about 60% of DRAM output) adds cost and delivery risk. The contracted floor helps but covers a minority of revenue. Evidence on both sides, leaning for: Contested at 0.58.

TTM operating cash flow less capex is $58.963bn against a $52.99bn test and a $26.49bn kill (prep evidence 2). The claim's point is right for the near term. Price-driven revenue needed little capital in FY2026: revenue up $95.8bn on $30.71bn of capex. So the code's year-1 free cash flow to the firm of $26.495bn understates cash generation while prices hold. The test runs to August 2028, though, and three things in the dossier work against it. Capex is guided at about $25bn net of incentives in the first half of FY2027 alone and higher after. Cash taxes of $1.25bn against a $14.8bn provision will catch up. Receivables rose $25.2bn. So FY2028 needs operating cash flow of roughly twice FY2026's capex, and that probably needs operating income near C2's line. That makes C3 at least as hard as C2. R5 points the same way: in 2017-2025 operating cash flow less capex was only $15.9bn, and spending follows price. A downturn would release working capital and capex can be cut, as in 2023, which keeps this near even. Contested at 0.45.

red_flags.reasoning: The flag says earnings and margins are at a shortage peak and price-driven. Its only rebuttal claim, C2, is Contested, not Supported, so the flag stands. The evidence says FY2026 is not the trailing peak, since the November quarter is guided higher. It does not show that the shortage price will survive the supply arriving in 2027-28.

mispricing_reason: The market view's facts check out. The price implies 17.22% growth a year on the code's fade, and EV is 7.45 times TTM EBIT. But the claim that the market is wrong rests on C1, which I put at 0.45, with C2 and C3 Contested too. On the effective base case the price of $690 is only 5.3% under the DCF value of $728.75, for 7.46% a year. Pricing a margin collapse is what the market did correctly in 2018 and 2022, when low trailing multiples came before falls in earnings. The new contracts are real but cover a minority of revenue. So the evidence does not show a mispricing.
p_intact_reason: All three claims are in scope through their kills, which apply now. No test is due within 12 months (review_by 2028-10-31). Each kill needs two consecutive quarter-ends in breach. The quarters reported by November 2027 run to August 2027, and the TTM figures then include the guided November 2026 quarter and the consensus February 2027 quarter, both at record levels. For C1's TTM margin to fall below 46.28%, C2's TTM operating income below $85bn, or C3's TTM operating cash flow less capex below $26.49bn at two quarter-ends by then, the cycle would have to collapse within about two quarters of a record guide. That is faster than the 2022-23 fall, when TTM EBIT took three quarters to drop 81%. The Red Team's leading indicators would warn first: a quarterly margin under 70%, a cut in FY2027 EPS consensus, or negative DRAM contract prices. Residual risk is a sharp 2027 break plus cash taxes and capex catching up for C3, and measurement noise in the cache's quarterly cash flow. The Red Team was blind, so its case is weighed in full.
verdict_reason: Pursue fails. The effective base-case return is 7.46%, below 12%, because no deviation claim is Supported. The severe flag is unresolved, the mispricing does not hold and no claim is Supported. The rule then gives watch: the core claim is Contested, not Unsupported, no kill that applies today is breached, and the business is sound on ROIC (110.54% against a 9.37% discount rate). The next evidence is the November-quarter results due 16 Dec 2026.

kill_criteria.criterion: TTM operating margin below 46.28% at two consecutive quarter-ends before the August 2028 quarter's results: the margin would be fading faster than the code's own path and the price-band contracts would not have changed the cycle.
TTM operating income below $85bn at two consecutive quarter-ends: FY2026's earnings would have been the peak and the cyclical fall not stopped by the contracts.
TTM operating cash flow less capex below $26.49bn, the code's year-1 free cash flow to the firm, at two consecutive quarter-ends: the code's reinvestment charge would be right.

deviations: No base_rate_deviation claim is Supported, so the base case is the code's (7.46% a year) and no override is applied.

judge_prep.json was read as written on 2026-11-07 (run.yaml judge_prep: keep) and not rebuilt today. Its recompute, macro values and price (6 Nov close of $690) are as of then. Logged in runs/2026-11-07-semis/judge/issues.tsv.
The Red Team was blind (no claims.json at its commit), so no blindness caveat applies.
